parts.title: Notices, signs and messages
parts.instruction: Read the six short texts and questions 1-6. For each question, choose the correct answer: A, B or C.

texts.label: Text 1
texts.title: Hartley Library
paras: If you need to return books, please use the box by the main door. Late books cost 20p a day.

texts.label: Text 2
texts.title: Message from Tom to Amira
paras: Hi Amira, I'm at the station but the 5.15 train has been cancelled. The next one is at 5.45, so I'll be late for dinner. Please start without me! Tom

texts.label: Text 4
texts.title: Email from Greenfield Sports Centre
paras: Dear members, the swimming pool will be closed from 3 to 7 June for cleaning. The gym and the café will stay open as usual. Sorry for any problems.

texts.label: Text 5
texts.title: Note from Zofia to Kwame
paras: Hi Kwame, a parcel came for you this morning and I took it. I'm out until six, but my husband is at home all day. Just knock on the door of number 14. Zofia

texts.label: Text 6
texts.title: Park Café
paras: Dogs are welcome in our garden.
Dogs are not allowed inside the café.

items.question: What can you do when the library is closed?
options: Put books in the box by the door.
Take books out of the box.
items.why: The notice says to use the box by the main door to return books.

items.question: Why is Tom writing to Amira?
options: To say that he will be late.
To ask her to meet him at the station.
items.why: His train was cancelled, so he will be late for dinner.

items.question: How much are jeans in the sale?
items.why: The notice says: Jeans: £10.

items.question: What can members do between 3 and 7 June?
items.why: Only the pool is closed; the gym stays open as usual.

items.question: What should Kwame do?
options: Go to number 14 to get his parcel.
Wait until six o'clock to collect it.
Take the parcel to the post office.
items.why: Zofia's husband is at home all day, so Kwame can knock on the door of number 14.

items.question: Where can people take their dogs?
options: Into the garden and the café.
Into the garden, but not into the café.
Into the café, but not into the garden.
items.why: Dogs are welcome in the garden but not allowed inside the café.

parts.title: Three people, one topic
parts.instruction: Read the three texts about learning a musical instrument and questions 7-13. For each question, choose the correct answer: A, B or C. You can choose any letter more than once.

a.title: A - Priya
a.body: I started playing the piano two years ago, when I was 28. I have a lesson every Thursday evening with a teacher who comes to my flat, and I practise for twenty minutes every morning before work. My neighbours don't mind because I use headphones with my electric piano. My dream is to play at my sister's wedding next year.

b.title: B - Liam
b.body: My grandfather gave me his old guitar when I was ten, so I learnt from videos online. I don't have lessons. I play in a small band with three friends from work, and we practise every Sunday in Dan's garage. We have never played for an audience, but we are going to play in a café next month. I'm a bit nervous!

c.title: C - Mei
c.body: I have played the violin since I was six. Now I teach it to children after school. I like teaching, but my favourite thing is the orchestra in our town, where I play every Tuesday. We give four concerts a year. I don't practise much at home because I'm too tired after work.

items.prompt: Who was given an instrument by a relative?
Who will play in front of people for the first time soon?
Who would like to play at a family event?
Who is often too tired to practise at home?
Who uses headphones so the neighbours can't hear?

parts.title: A magazine article
parts.instruction: Read the article about a baker and questions 14-18. For each question, choose the correct answer: A, B or C.

texts.label: Magazine
texts.title: From teacher to baker
paras: Hannah Cole was a primary school teacher for eight years. She liked her job, but she was always tired and had little time for her hobby, baking. 'Every Sunday I made bread and cakes for my family and neighbours,' she says. 'One day my neighbour said, You should sell these! I laughed, but I couldn't stop thinking about it.'

Last spring, Hannah left the school and rented a small shop in the centre of Whitby. She painted the walls yellow herself, and her brother built the shelves. The bakery opened in May, and on the first day she sold all her bread by ten o'clock.

Now Hannah gets up at four every morning. She bakes until seven, and then her helper, a student called Ravi, arrives to serve the customers. The bakery is open from eight to four, Tuesday to Saturday. 'Some people think I'm crazy,' says Hannah. 'I work longer hours than before, and I earn less money. But I'm much happier.'

Her most popular product is a cheese and onion loaf. Hannah's next idea is a small café with tables outside, where customers can eat cake and drink tea. 'I'd like to do it one day,' she says. 'First I need to find more space.'

items.question: Before she opened the bakery, Hannah
items.why: She was a primary school teacher for eight years.

items.question: Who built the shelves in the shop?
items.why: Hannah painted the walls herself, and her brother built the shelves.

items.question: What happened on the first day?
options: Hannah sold all her bread early.
Hannah closed the shop at ten o'clock.
items.why: She sold all her bread by ten o'clock.

items.question: What does Hannah say about her new life?
options: She earns more money than before.
She works more hours but is happier.
She is less happy than before.
items.why: She works longer hours and earns less, but she is much happier.

items.question: What would Hannah like to do in the future?
options: Sell her bread in other towns.
Open a café with tables outside.
items.why: Her next idea is a small café with tables outside.

parts.title: Choose the missing word
parts.instruction: Read the email and choose the correct word for each space (questions 19-24). For each question, choose the correct answer: A, B or C.

segments.t: Hi Zofia,
Greetings from Edinburgh! We
in Edinburgh on Friday evening, and the weather has been lovely so
. Yesterday we walked up a big hill called Arthur's Seat. The
from the top was amazing! In the afternoon we
a bus tour round the city. Tom wanted to see the castle, but it was
when we got there, so we'll go tomorrow.
Tonight we're having dinner in a small restaurant near our hotel. I hope you and Ravi
well. See you next week!
Love, Amira

items.why: We say 'arrive in' a city; 'reached in' and 'came in' do not fit.
'So far' means 'until now'.
You see a view from the top of a hill.
We 'take' a bus tour.
A castle can be closed to visitors; it cannot be 'lost' or 'ended'.
'You and Ravi' is plural, so we need 'are'.

parts.title: Write the missing word
parts.instruction: Read the email and write ONE word for each space (questions 25-30).

segments.t: Hi Kwame,
Thanks
your message. I'm really glad you can come to my birthday party on Saturday! It starts
seven o'clock. You can come by train, but it is easier
take the bus. The number 12 stops
front of my building.
will be about twenty people, so it will be a big party. I hope
like pizza, because we are ordering a lot!
See you on Saturday,
Tara

items.why: 'Thanks for' + noun.
We use 'at' with clock times.
'It is easier to + verb'.
The fixed phrase is 'in front of'.
'There will be' says that something exists.
'I hope you like pizza' - the subject is 'you'.

parts.title: Write an email
parts.instruction: Question 1. Read the situation and write your email. Write 25 words or more. Write about all three things.

tasks.title: Question 1 · Email to a friend
tasks.situation: Your English friend Alex has invited you to stay with him next weekend.
points: Say what you would like to do.
tasks.model:
Hi Alex,
Thank you for inviting me! I can arrive on Saturday at about ten o'clock. I would like to visit the new museum and then have lunch in the park. What clothes should I bring?
See you soon,
Mei
checklist: Content: all three points are covered - when you can arrive, what you would like to do, and a question about clothes.
Organisation: a greeting (Hi Alex), short clear sentences and a closing (See you soon / Love).
Language: simple correct sentences; 'I can ...', 'I would like to ...' and a question with 'What ... should I ...?'
Length: 25 words or more. Writing about only one or two points loses marks for content.

parts.title: Write a story
parts.instruction: Question 2. Look at the three pictures (described below) and write the story. Write 35 words or more.

tasks.title: Question 2 · Picture story
tasks.situation:
Picture 1: It is raining. A woman called Maya is waiting at a bus stop with an umbrella. She looks cold and unhappy.
Picture 2: A car stops next to the bus stop. Maya's friend Ben is driving. He opens the door for her.
Picture 3: Maya and Ben are in the car. They are laughing. A cinema is in front of them.
tasks.prompt: Write the story shown in the three pictures.
points: Say what is happening in picture 1.
Say what is happening in picture 2.
Say how the story ends in picture 3.
tasks.model: It was raining and Maya was waiting at the bus stop. She was cold and wet. Then she saw her friend Ben in his car. He stopped and opened the door for her. Now Maya and Ben are driving to the cinema and they are laughing.
checklist: Content: the story covers all three pictures in the right order.
Organisation: simple linking words (then, and, but, now) so the sentences form a story.
Language: past tenses (was waiting, saw, stopped) or present tenses used consistently; weather and travel words.

parts.title: Five short recordings
parts.instruction: Questions 1-5. You will hear five short recordings. You will hear each recording twice. For each question, choose the correct answer: A, B or C. (The real exam uses pictures here; we use short text options instead.)

script.t: Shall we go to the cinema tonight? I've checked the website, and the film starts at half past seven, not seven o'clock.
Half past seven is fine. I finish work at six, so there's plenty of time to get there.
Hi Amira, it's Tom. It's about tomorrow's trip to the lake. The forecast is good, so you won't need your raincoat. But please bring some sun cream. I'll bring the sandwiches. See you at nine!
Excuse me, do you have these boots in a size six?
Let me check. I'm sorry, we only have black in size five and size seven. But we do have size six in brown.
Brown is fine, actually. I'll take them.
Attention, please. The ten fifteen train to Leeds will now leave from platform six, not platform three. Please go to platform six. The train is running ten minutes late. We are sorry for the delay.
Are we still having the barbecue on Saturday?
Yes. I heard it's going to rain in the morning, but it will be dry and sunny after lunch. So let's start at three.

items.question: What time does the film start?
items.why: The woman says half past seven, not seven o'clock.

items.question: What must Amira bring?
items.why: Tom says she won't need a raincoat, he will bring the sandwiches, and she should bring sun cream.

items.question: Which boots does the woman buy?
items.why: The only size six is brown, and she says she will take them.

items.question: Which platform does the Leeds train leave from?
items.why: It leaves from platform six, not platform three. Ten is the number of minutes it is late.

items.question: When will the weather be good on Saturday?
items.why: It rains in the morning but is dry and sunny after lunch.

parts.title: Complete the notes
parts.instruction: Questions 6-10. You will hear a woman leaving a message about a pottery class. For each question, write the correct answer in the gap. Write ONE word or a number or a date or a time. You will hear the recording twice.

script.t: Hello, this is Karen from Riverside Community Centre. You asked about our pottery class for beginners. There is a Tuesday class, but it's full, so I've put you on the Thursday class instead. It starts on the twelfth of October at seven o'clock in the evening, and it lasts for eight weeks.

The course costs ninety-six pounds, and that includes the clay. The teacher is Mr Okafor. That's O-K-A-F-O-R. Please bring an apron, but you don't need to bring any tools. If you'd like to book, please call me back before Friday. Thank you. Goodbye.

items.why: Tuesday is full, so she is on the Thursday class.
The class starts at seven o'clock in the evening.
The course costs ninety-six pounds.
The name is spelt O-K-A-F-O-R.
She says to bring an apron but no tools.

parts.title: A conversation about a new flat
parts.instruction: Questions 11-15. You will hear a conversation between a man, Liam, and a woman, Mei, about her new flat. For each question, choose the correct answer: A, B or C. You will hear the conversation twice.

script.t: Hi Mei! How's the new flat?
Hi Liam. It's really nice, thanks. I moved in two weeks ago, and I'm still unpacking boxes!
Is it far from your old place?
Not really, only about two kilometres. But it's much nearer my office. I used to take two buses to work, and now I can walk there in fifteen minutes.
That's great. And what about the flat itself?
It has two bedrooms, so I use the small one as an office. There's no garden, but there's a lovely park across the road.
Do you like your neighbours?
I've only met one so far, an older man called Mr Evans who lives downstairs. He's very friendly. He brought me a cake on the first day!
How kind! When can I come and see it?
How about this Saturday? I'm having a small party in the evening, but you could come in the afternoon and help me put up some shelves.
Sure, I'm free after two o'clock. Shall I bring my tools?
Yes, please. That would be brilliant. I only have a very small screwdriver.

items.question: How long has Mei lived in the flat?
items.why: She moved in two weeks ago.

items.question: How does Mei go to work now?
items.why: She used to take two buses, but now she walks in fifteen minutes.

items.question: What does Mei use the small bedroom for?
items.why: She says she uses the small one as an office.

items.question: What does Mei say about Mr Evans?
items.why: He brought her a cake on the first day; he lives downstairs.

items.question: What will Liam do on Saturday?
items.why: He will come in the afternoon with his tools to help put up shelves.

parts.title: Five short conversations and messages
parts.instruction: Questions 16-20. You will hear five short recordings. For each question, choose the correct answer: A, B or C. You will hear each recording twice.

script.t: Hello, Mr Singh, this is Bella at Parkside Dental Practice. Dr Hughes is ill on Wednesday, so we can't see you at three o'clock. Could you come on Thursday at the same time instead? Please call us back on 01632 960 331 to say if that's all right. Thank you.
Good evening. Do you have a table for two, please?
I have one outside now, but it's a bit cold. Or I can give you a table by the window in about ten minutes.
It's too cold outside. We'll wait for the table by the window, thank you.

Good morning, everyone. A quick reminder about tomorrow's trip to the museum. The coach will leave at half past eight, not at nine as it said in the letter. Please bring a packed lunch and wear comfortable shoes. You don't need any money, because the museum is free.
Did you watch the football last night?
Yes, but I didn't enjoy the first half. Nothing happened. The last twenty minutes were really exciting, though.

Hi Ravi, it's me. Sorry, I'm going to be about twenty minutes late. It's not the bus, I caught that one. There's been an accident on the High Street and the traffic isn't moving. Please start without me.

items.question: What is the message about?
items.why: The practice asks him to come on Thursday instead of Wednesday.

items.question: What does the man decide to do?
options: Wait for a table by the window
items.why: It is too cold outside, so they will wait for the window table.

items.question: What does the speaker tell the students about the trip?
options: It will start earlier than planned.
It will cost more than planned.
items.why: The coach leaves at half past eight, not at nine.

items.question: What does the man think of the match?
options: It was boring all the way through.
It got better at the end.
items.why: The first half was dull, but the last twenty minutes were exciting.

items.question: Why will the woman be late?
options: There is a lot of traffic.
items.why: She says she caught the bus but the traffic isn't moving after an accident.

parts.title: Matching: presents
parts.instruction: Questions 21-25. You will hear Kwame and Mei talking about presents for Kwame's family. What present is Kwame giving to each person? For each question, choose the correct letter, A-H. You will hear the conversation twice. There are three letters you do not need.

script.t: Have you finished your present shopping, Kwame?
Nearly. For my mum, I was thinking of a mug, because she loves tea. But she already has about twenty, so I bought her a small plant for the kitchen.
Lovely. And your dad?
That was hard. I almost bought him a watch, but he never wears one. In the end I found a cookery book with recipes from Italy. He loves cooking.
And your sister?
Amira? I thought about a board game, but she would much rather have headphones. Hers are broken.
What about your grandmother?
She always feels the cold, so I got her a scarf. It's dark green.
And your uncle Ben?
Chocolates. He has a sweet tooth, and I always give him chocolates.

parts.title: Interview
parts.instruction: The examiner asks you some questions about yourself, your daily life and your interests. Answer each question with a full sentence and try to add one more detail. Then your partner answers questions too. (In the real exam this part lasts about 3-4 minutes.)

tasks.title: Part 1 · Questions about you
tasks.situation: The examiner asks you and your partner questions. Practise answering these aloud.

card.title: Examiner's questions
lines: What's your name? How do you spell your surname?
Where do you live? Do you like living there?
What do you do - do you work or study?
What do you usually do at the weekend?
Tell me about your family or your best friend.
What did you do last weekend?

redemittel: My name is ... and I'm from ...
I live in ... It's a quiet / busy / friendly place.
I work as a ... / I'm a student of ...
At the weekend I usually ... with my friends.
Last weekend I went to ... and I ...
tasks.model:
Examiner: What's your name?
Mei: My name is Mei Lin. That's M-E-I, and Lin is L-I-N.
Examiner: Where do you live?
Mei: I live in Manchester, in a small flat near the centre. I like it because there are lots of shops and cafés.
Examiner: Do you work or study?
Mei: I work in a bookshop. I start at nine and finish at five.
Examiner: What do you usually do at the weekend?
Mei: I usually see my friends. Sometimes we go to the cinema, and on Sundays I cook dinner for my family.
Examiner: What did you do last weekend?
Mei: I went to a market with my sister and bought some vegetables. Then we cooked together.
checklist: Task: you answer every question and say a little more than one word.
Interaction: you listen to the question and your answer fits it; you can spell your name.
Language: simple present for routines, simple past for last weekend, everyday vocabulary.
Pronunciation: clear enough to understand; word stress and sentence rhythm.

parts.title: Discussion with pictures
parts.instruction: You and your partner talk together. The examiner gives you a sheet with pictures (described below). Talk about the pictures and decide which one is best. Then the examiner asks you each a few more questions. (In the real exam this part lasts about 5-6 minutes.)

tasks.title: Part 2 · A birthday for a friend
tasks.situation: A friend has a birthday next week. You and your partner want to do something special together. Talk about the different things you can do and decide which is best.

card.title: What can we do for our friend's birthday?
lines: Picture 2: a trip to the cinema
Picture 3: a picnic in the park
Picture 5: a visit to a museum

redemittel: I think a ... would be good because ...
I don't think ... is a good idea because it's too ...
tasks.model:
A: What do you think about the restaurant?
B: A meal is nice, but it can be expensive. How about a picnic in the park?
A: That's a good idea, but the weather might be bad. What about bowling? It's fun with a group.
B: Yes, our friend loves games, and we can all join in. Afterwards we can have pizza.
A: Great. Let's choose bowling. Do you agree?
B: Yes, I agree.
Examiner (to A): Do you like birthday parties? Why / why not?
A: Yes, I do. I like seeing all my friends together, and I like the cake!
Examiner (to B): What did you do on your last birthday?
B: I had dinner at home with my family. My mum made my favourite food.
checklist: Task: you talk about most of the pictures, give reasons and agree on one idea.
Interaction: you ask your partner questions, react to what they say, and do not just give a list.
Language: suggestions (How about ...? Let's ...), opinions with 'because', and a few linking words (but, and, so).
Pronunciation: clear and easy to follow; use question intonation when you ask your partner.
